aiOverview.content: President Trump fired Attorney General Pam Bondi in April 2026 after a 14-month tenure, primarily due to frustration over her failure to aggressively prosecute his political enemies and "limited success" in acting on his grievances. Despite her loyalty, Trump was dissatisfied with her performance, the pace of investigations, and handling of Epstein-related files. Key reasons for her firing include: Lack of Prosecutions: Trump was annoyed by her inability to secure indictments against perceived enemies, including cases involving former FBI Director James Comey and NY Attorney General Letitia James. Performance Frustration: The President felt she failed to fully "execute on his vision" and manage the Justice Department as a tool for retribution. Epstein Files Handling: Early stumbles in managing the release of Jeffrey Epstein-related files created political liabilities. Desire for a New Direction: Trump wanted a more aggressive approach, prompting consideration of replacing her with more combative, trusted allies. She was replaced on an acting basis by Todd Blanche.
